Everything on the truck that tastes of something starts here. Bought stock is salt water with a picture of a chicken on it.

## Why bother

Numbers from October 2024: we go through about 18 litres a week between the short rib braise, the gravy for the Sunday rolls and the noodle broth. Knorr Professional paste for that volume was costing £27 a week. Bones from Hollis & Sons in Chorlton are £1.20 a kilo, carcasses free if I take them on a Tuesday. Doing it ourselves is about £9 a week plus gas. That's £936 a year back in the till, and it's better.

## Brown chicken stock

- 5 kg chicken carcasses and wings, roasted 200°C for 45 min until properly brown, not tan
- 1 kg onion, 500 g carrot, 500 g celery, roughly 2:1:1, chopped big
- 2 tbsp tomato purée, fried off in the roasting tray
- 1 head garlic cut across, 10 peppercorns, 3 bay, a handful of parsley stalks
- 8 L cold water

Deglaze the roasting tray with a litre of the water and scrape every bit of brown in. That tray is half the flavour.

## Beef brown stock

Same method, 6 kg beef shin bones and knuckles, roasted 220°C for an hour. Add 2 pig trotters halved by Frank at Hollis for body. 10 L water. This one gets 10 to 12 hours. It's the base for the braise in [[Braised short ribs]] and the jus.

## Ratios I actually use

- bones to water 1:1.6 by weight for chicken, 1:1.7 for beef
- mirepoix 20% of bone weight, any more and it goes sweet
- no salt. Ever. It gets reduced later and you can't take salt out
- reduction target: 8 L down to about 5 L finished

## Timeline for a Sunday batch

- 07:00 bones in the oven at the commissary in Openshaw (unit 7)
- 08:00 into the 40 L stockpot, cold water, bring up slowly
- 08:45 first skim, then every 30 min for 2 hours
- 09:00 veg in
- chicken off at 13:00, beef left overnight on the lowest setting with the lid half on
- strain through a chinois, then muslin

## Clarity and skimming

Never boil it. A tremble, one bubble every second or two, about 90 to 95°C on the probe. Boil it and the fat emulsifies in and it goes cloudy and greasy. If it does go cloudy I don't bother with a raft, it's going into a braise anyway, but for the noodle broth I do an egg white raft: 4 whites per 3 L, plus 200 g minced chicken.

## Storage and labels

- cool in the blast chiller to under 5°C within 90 min (EHO checked this in Feb 2025, passed)
- 1 L deli tubs, labelled STK-C or STK-B plus the date
- fridge 4 days, freezer 3 months
- reduced to glace (10:1) it keeps 3 weeks in the fridge and is what makes [[Pan sauce basics]] work

## Scraps and waste

Strained bones and veg go in the food waste bin for the council collection, the veg-only bits (onion skins, carrot ends) go to my mum's [[Compost pile]] in Stockport. She complains about the onion skins. She can complain.

## Dashi variant

For the noodle broth I sometimes swap half the chicken stock for kombu dashi: 20 g kombu per litre, cold soak overnight, 60°C for an hour. A spoon of the white miso from [[Miso koji]] at the end makes it.

## Cost per litre

- chicken: £0.48
- beef: £0.71
- dashi: £0.92 because kombu is daylight robbery
